context_summary: F07 Front-end Dashboard — full create-feature pipeline execution. The Architect plan (approved in D-20260818-007) is ready with 8 tasks across 4 waves: scaffolding, core pages, detail pages, and polish. The F06 REST API backend is stable with 385 tests at 96% coverage, CORS enabled, and OpenAPI docs.

options_considered.description: Proceed with the full create-feature pipeline (Readiness check, TEA, Waves 0-3, TechLead review, QA validation). Execute all 8 tasks as planned.
pros: The Architect plan is well-structured with clear wave dependencies — scaffolding before pages, pages before polish
F06 REST API is fully tested and stable — the front-end has a reliable backend to consume
CORS already enabled with allow_origins=['*'] — no backend modifications needed
Tech stack (Vite + React + TypeScript + Tailwind) is mainstream with excellent tooling support
The plan explicitly scopes out risky features (auth, portfolio, AI) — clean MVP boundaries
All 8 tasks have clear acceptance criteria in the task files
cons: Introduces Node.js toolchain as a new dependency in the mono-repo
8 tasks across 4 waves is a full pipeline run — significant token cost
Front-end tests (Vitest + RTL) are a new test stack separate from the Python pytest suite

options_considered.description: Defer execution. Request the Architect to slim the plan down to 4 tasks (2 waves) covering only scaffolding and one core page before committing to the full 8-task pipeline.
pros: Smaller blast radius — validates the new tech stack with fewer tasks before going all-in
Lower token cost for initial validation
cons: The plan is already well-scoped with no-auth, no-portfolio, no-AI boundaries — it is already minimal
Wave 0 (scaffolding) already serves as the validation step — if it fails, later waves naturally stop
Splitting an already-planned feature wastes the Architect work done in D-20260818-007
The user requested the full pipeline, not an incremental approach

rationale: The plan is already well-scoped and minimal — 4 pages, no auth, no portfolio, no AI. Wave 0 (scaffolding + API client) naturally validates the new tech stack before subsequent waves build on it. The F06 backend is stable and CORS-ready, so there are no blocking dependencies. Proceeding with the full pipeline is the right call since the Architect plan was already approved and the wave structure provides natural checkpoints.
